title: Share experiment plumbing without sharing scientific evaluators
claim: The exact World Zero, Mosaic, and DriftGuard subjects do not justify a shared experiment harness or generic receipt schema. The original World Zero↔Mosaic four-part receipt residue does not survive a materially independent DriftGuard implementation: repository-source subject identity, general execution context, and explicit claim-ceiling fields are not common across all three. Keep experiment/qualification receipts project-specific.
preserved_boundaries: World Zero owns its scientific model, domain variables, calibration/holdout logic, and scientific claims.
Mosaic owns its continuity/specialist hypothesis, accelerator/runtime assumptions, and success criteria.
Shared mechanics may record and replay experiments but cannot determine scientific validity.
promotion_evidence: World Zero RUN_RECEIPT_V1 blob 88a039e32e3cbcb4e26aa9a95cc2f0d817ca1423 binds scientific subject identity, source commit/tree, dataset/parameter/region/scenario/observation digests, calibration and holdout partitions, comparison protocol digest, solver identity, seed, tolerance, timestep, environment fingerprint, and optional result digest.

World Zero comparison protocol blob c0580445f322fb3b91ad0619eb30502414803d55 freezes subjects, calibration/holdout partitions, metrics, decision rules, missing-subject policy, and confirmatory-versus-exploratory status.

Mosaic harness blob ab880ada80dd238751f7aec918cd0cafb5e85ce9 instead executes four continuity conditions over revisioned state events and emits continuity-specific accuracy, stale-error, correction-burden, payload-size, unload/latency/repeatability gates, and an explicit P1 claim ceiling.
Mosaic test blob ebf4851bacfbbab71b7a6ad664ef232123fd91bd verifies the harness cannot self-award P1 and that ordinary retrieval receives no special disadvantage.
Third-consumer falsifier binds DriftGuard main@9894692ff6b549e4378bcc2b8ca46813ff18bf37 and its DRIFTGUARD_RECOVERY_WINDOW_RECEIPT_V1 implementation blob af329f61d9eb9f094896a4eb14f1263d9f6c861a.

DriftGuard's receipt subject is state/session/ledger recovery-window identity, not repository-source experiment identity; its policy/turn/generation window is not a general execution-environment record.

Across World Zero, Mosaic, and DriftGuard, only result/evidence identity survives cleanly; exact repository source subject, general execution context, and explicit claim-ceiling receipt fields do not.
No common layer has deleted or replaced existing project-local code: demonstrated_code_deleted_or_replaced_by_common_layer = 0.
rejection_conditions: A common harness requires either project's domain ontology or evaluator.
The adapter layer is larger than the duplicated experiment plumbing removed.
Shared result types encourage one project's validity criteria to leak into the other.
Either project can no longer execute independently.

critical_objections: Shrinking the common record to id/digest/status would be serialization, not meaningful shared experiment architecture.
DriftGuard's durable ledger-bound receipt cannot be normalized into a World Zero scientific run receipt without losing subject semantics.
Mosaic's synthetic continuity receipt lacks the general source/execution identity required by the prior residue.
No extraction has demonstrated real code deletion or reduced maintenance burden.

notes: Pairwise experiment result: PROJECT_SPECIFIC for executable harnesses.
No shared code or shared harness schema is proposed from this pair.
Third materially independent consumer tested: DriftGuard. The prior four-part generic receipt residue failed the three-way intersection.
Disposition remains PROJECT_SPECIFIC / NO_EXTRACTION. No generic receipt candidate is created.
